subject: scantwo issue due to large vector size

messages.author: 2be6be143f022015
messages.subject: scantwo issue due to large vector size
parts:
Hello,

I am trying to run scantwo using Drosophila recombinant inbred lines, I have 256 lines and 6624 markers. When I try to run scantwo I encounter a problem with the vector being too large (~13.2GB), and from what I was able to find it seems like R itself only handle vectors up to 8GB. I tried to downsize my data set by droping whole chromosome arms and went down to 1239 markers, but the vector produced by scantwo didn't reduce in size at all. 

I was surprised that reducing the number of markers didn't have an effect on vector size. When I calculate genotype probabilities I am using step size 0, since the data set is already dense. Are there options to try to avoid having this issue and use scantwo or should I just try a different approach on my mapping experiment? My next attempt would be to perform multi-QTL.

example code:
> ril_gp <- calc.genoprob(ril_data,step=0, err=0.001)
> etoh_s2 <- scantwo( ril_gp   , verbose = FALSE, method="em")

Thanks in advance for any help.

Best,
--   

Best,

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] scantwo issue due to large vector size
parts:
In reducing from 6624 markers to 1239, you're going down by a factor of 5, so the requested vector size from scantwo should go down by a factor of 25.
The 1239 marker case should be do-able. You'd probably want to use method="hk" rather than method="em", for speed.

I'm kind of surprised that you can't do 6624 markers. I'd have thought it would use more like 6624*6624*8 bytes = about 350 MB.

karl
